figures.caption: Fig. 1: Comparison between conventional post-hoc HMM inference and the proposed CRF framework. In the post-hoc pipeline (top), the AAD backbone is trained only with window-level CE and remains fixed when the HMM is applied. In our framework (bottom), the backbone outputs neural emissions for a Markov CRF, and the sequence-level objective backpropagates through the CRF into the backbone. The resulting emissions support both causal and non-causal decoding.

Fig. 4: Per-participant Acc. improvement of CRF over HMM-post on AVGC using ESCNet emissions (1 s window). Bar, dot and dashed line show participant-mean, fold-level and overall-mean gains (%), respectively.

Fig. 5: Paired statistical test of CRF versus HMM-post. Positive values indicate that end-to-end Markov training improves over HMM post-processing, and vice versa. Significance stars use Holm-Bonferroni corrected p-values across all eight tests.
